slides.title:
Contrast drift:
signal or correction?
slides.subtitle:
A stability story built from invented traces.
Synthetic, dimensionless and nonclinical.
slides.notes: This seminar examines identifiability using invented normalized contrast signals. Dark and light are labels of toy conditions, not validated display modes or human-perception results. Every trace and tolerance is synthetic.

slides.title: Two toy conditions drift in opposite directions
slides.subtitle: 12 synthetic traces per condition; 11 ordered time steps each
slides.caption: SYN-D. Shared 0-1 axis; thin lines = traces; thick line = mean.
slides.interpretation: The drift is known because the generator put it there.
slides.notes: Time is a dimensionless simulation step, not minutes. The baseline is 0.32 for dark and 0.72 for light with trace-specific offsets and independent Gaussian noise. Twelve traces are not 132 independent experiments: each trace contains 11 repeated values.

slides.title: A flat curve can mean two different things
slides.subtitle: Native comparison separates a toy transformation from an earned explanation

left.title: Oracle correction
bullets: Subtract the exact drift used by the generator.
Not an estimator learned from unknown signals.

right.title: Independent estimation
bullets: Would need a separate reference channel.
Must preserve signal changes, not just flatten curves.
Not implemented or evaluated in this example.

slides.verdict: Known injected drift is privileged information, not measured reference evidence.
slides.notes: No claim of an operational drift-correction algorithm is made. An independent reference is a proposed evidence need, not an existing dataset. Keep the explicit oracle disclosure visible rather than hiding it in a caption.

slides.title: Subtracting injected drift restores the toy baseline
slides.subtitle: Same 12 dark-condition traces before and after oracle correction

figures.label: A
figures.title: Mean contrast trajectories
figures.caption: Raw and oracle-corrected means; n = 12 paired traces.

slides.caption: SYN-D. Horizontal line = invented baseline 0.32.
slides.interpretation: Recoverability under known drift is not identifiability under unknown drift.
slides.notes: Correction removes only drift*time, not the per-trace offset or measurement noise. The figure plots raw and corrected means on the full 0-1 scale. The result is expected by construction.

slides.title: Endpoint error shrinks by construction
slides.subtitle: Synthetic mean absolute endpoint change from time zero; n = 12 per condition
slides.caption: SYN-D. Paired absolute changes; dimensionless. Bars start at zero; no statistical test.
slides.notes: Compute each trace's absolute endpoint-minus-start difference first, then average the 12 values. This differs from taking the absolute difference between group means. The JSON ledger retains both raw and corrected arrays. No confidence interval, performance validation or perception claim is implied.

slides.title: Endpoint agreement hides the path
slides.subtitle: Synthetic corrected trajectories still contain trace-level variation
slides.caption: SYN-D. Dark condition; deviations from each trace's time-zero value; n = 12.

sidebar_sections.title: Readout
sidebar_sections.body: Noise remains after the known drift is removed.

sidebar_sections.title: Boundary
sidebar_sections.body: The +/-0.08 band is invented, not a display tolerance.

sidebar_sections.title: Missing
sidebar_sections.body: No reference channel or perceptual outcome is modeled.

slides.notes: The thin traces are not uncertainty intervals. A compact endpoint summary cannot establish stability throughout the complete sequence. The sidebar has three short sections at a 16-point requested floor.

slides.title: A useful next test withholds the drift law
slides.subtitle: Proposed synthetic extension, not completed work

flow_steps.title: Hide the law
flow_steps.detail: Keep injected drift unavailable to the estimator.

flow_steps.title: Add a reference
flow_steps.detail: Generate a separate noisy channel; freeze the estimator.

flow_steps.title: Challenge it
flow_steps.detail: Add a true signal change and check whether it survives correction.

slides.caption: SYN-D. Three native editable method bands.
slides.notes: This plan is intentionally not implemented in the generator. It marks the boundary of the example rather than silently extending the proof to a correction algorithm.

slides.title: Keep the demonstration; reject the stability claim
slides.subtitle: Synthetic seminar conclusion: the inference matters more than the flat line
bullets: Use the oracle case to explain the algebra of drift removal.
Do not claim an estimator, a stable device or improved perception.
Require a blinded reference-channel test before advancing the claim.
slides.summary_callout: The data are invented. The proposed reference-channel experiment has not been run.
slides.notes: This is a limitations-led seminar rather than a calibrated product recommendation. All 12 trace identities remain paired throughout the native chart and figure pipeline. The supported base preset currently uses a near-black page background; literal black figures are generated locally. Final color and geometry approval remain deferred.
